Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The Pakistani players are out in the middle. Tanzid Hasan and Saif Hassan to open for Bangladesh. Shaheen Afridi to bowl first. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

A great start by the visitors! Unlike the first game, where Pakistan played cautiously, the openers came out all guns blazing to put some early pressure on Bangladesh. Maaz Sadaqat, in particular, was outstanding today, scoring his maiden half-century in ODIs. However, Mehidy Hasan Miraz broke the 103-run partnership and was also at the thick of the action in the second 100-plus partnership.  Bangladesh have the momentum on their back and with their batters in confident touch after the first game, they'll be looking to chase it down. Pakistan need to make the most of the new ball. Stay tuned for the chase.

Pakistan's batting effort! At 231 for 3, Pakistan were eyeing a 300-plus score with Rizwan and Agha cruising. The 109-run partnership between Rizwan and Agha appeared to be the bedrock of a massive innings with both batters looking increasingly comfortable.  However, the game turned on its head following a highly controversial run-out decision involving Agha. The breakthrough proved catastrophic as Mohammad Rizwan followed him too, putting the innings in jeopardy. Eventually, Pakistan’s middle and lower order crumbled, losing their final five wickets for a mere 22 runs to finish well short of their projected target.

Innings highlight - A significantly improved batting performance from Pakistan, compared to their series opener, though they faced a late-innings wobble which ultimately cost them a promising total.  Bangladesh have the upper hand right now, but with a much better performance with the bat, Pakistan have given their bowlers plenty of runs to play with.

OUT! SALMAN AGHA IS RUN OUT! A huge moment in the game and a controversial one as well. Mehidy Hasan Miraz drops it short and on middle, Mohammad Rizwan punches it down the pitch. Mehidy moves to his right but Salman Agha gets in his way and the ball hits the non-striker's pad and stops. Agha bends down to pick up the ball and give it to the bowler, but before he can do that, Mehidy quickly grabs the ball and throws it at the stumps, with Agha standing out of his crease. There is an appeal for a run out, and even though Agha is not happy about it, the on-field umpire has to go upstairs. The replay shows that the batter is outside his crease and 'OUT' flashes on the big screen. Bangladesh were well within their rights to appeal for this, but the spirit of the game certainly takes a hit here. Salman is fuming, throws his gloves on the ground but he has to walk back here, and the big 109-run stand is broken now.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The conditions are a bit overcast in Dhaka but thankfully no signs of rain. Fans are still coming in the stadium and we can expect a full house for this game. Mehidy Hasan Miraz leads the Bangladesh players out to the middle before they take up their respective field positions. Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat are the two openers for Pakistan. Taskin Ahmed has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Two slips in place as well. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Athar Ali Khan is pitchside. He says that there is a lot more grass left on the wicket than the last game. Adds that the bowlers will target the 6-8 meter area to get help from the surface. Athar mentions that it is hard and compact but expects even bounce. Ends by saying that the batters will also enjoy playing their shots as the ball will come onto the bat nicely.

The middle order needs to step up - Shaheen Afridi, the skipper of Pakistan, says the wicket looks good, green on the surface and a little bit hard. Reckons their batters know their mistake, they come harder and play their shots, and Afridi fully believes in them. Shares that they started well with the bat in the last match, but want to play in the middle overs and get a big total. Informs Haris Rauf replaces Abrar Ahmed.

Focus on their process - Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the captain of Bangladesh, states that he expects his bowlers to click as they were ruthless in the last match. Continues that Nahid Rana did great, taking many wickets, which was a blessing. They're looking for wickets in the first 10 overs again. After being asked what are the plans for this match, he says that he would like to seal the series which won't be easy. All matches have been challenging. Miraz wants the team to focus on their process and as a batting unit, take responsibility to score runs. Miraz describes the pitch as a great wicket to bat on, and praises Tanzid's batting. He says bowling well makes things easier for a captain. Ends up by saying that there is no team changes and they're sticking with the same team.

A seven-year wait ends! Bangladesh's performance reflected a team hungry for success after their forced absence from the world stage. The hosts capitalized on Pakistan's inexperience batting line-up, but winning the toss made a huge impact on that game, regardless of the fact that Shaheen Afridi would have opted to bat first anyway. But the resilience of the bowling unit of this side was just impeccable. This victory was particularly historic as it was Bangladesh's first ODI win over Pakistan since the 2018 Asia Cup and their largest-ever win against them in terms of wickets and balls remaining. With the series lead, Bangladesh has successfully set a positive tone for their road to the 2027 World Cup, while Pakistan faces immediate pressure to find consistency among their new-look top order. So folks, fasten your seatbelt as this enthralling match will begin shortly. Toss and team updates to follow.

The rebuilt crisis? Pakistan entered the series following a disappointing loss against the Bangla Tigers. They had four debuts in the very first game, which is also their most in an ODI since 2008, as they are looking to rebuild their structure. Their struggle for stability was evident in the 1st ODI, where only four of their batters got to double digits, and the maximum was scored by Faheem Ashraf (37 off 47 deliveries). Even after losing the previous encounter, Pakistan still dominate the head-to-head record by winning 34 matches out of 39 ODIs, which basically sums up the heritage this side holds, but the question is, will the newcomers click in this do-or-die scenario?

Warm welcome to all the readers - The first ODI between Bangladesh and Pakistan in Mirpur marked a significant restart for both teams, as it was their first international encounter following the 2026 T20 World Cup phase. But today once again these Asian giants will lock their horns at the Shere Bangla National Stadium, where the Bangla Tigers will be looking forward to end the series by winning this clash, and on the other side, Pakistan's win will give them the chance to level it up.
... MATCHDAY ...

Series on the line in Mirpur - With the series on the line and plenty at stake beyond just this contest, Bangladesh and Pakistan return to the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur for the second ODI of the three-match series. The hosts carry strong momentum after a commanding eight-wicket win in the opener, where Bangladesh's bowling once again proved their biggest strength. Nahid Rana's fiery 5/24 ripped through Pakistan's inexperienced batting lineup, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz provided control through the middle overs before Tanzid Hasan's fluent 67 not out guided the chase with ease. Tigers roaring at home - Bangladesh have built a reputation in recent years for being extremely difficult to beat in home conditions, particularly on Mirpur's surfaces where their combination of seamers and spinners often thrives. Najmul Hossain Shanto will again be key at the top of the order, while captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz remains the side's most reliable all-round performer with his ability to influence games with both bat and ball. Litton Das also remains a crucial figure in the batting unit with his ability to anchor or accelerate depending on the situation, while Tawhid Hridoy's aggressive middle-order strokeplay could provide the momentum Bangladesh often look for in the middle overs. Firepower with the ball - With the ball, Mustafizur Rahman's variations and the raw pace of Nahid Rana give the hosts multiple wicket-taking options on a surface that showed signs of offering both seam movement and bounce in the first game. Taskin Ahmed's ability to hit the deck hard and extract extra bounce adds further bite to the pace attack, while leg-spinner Rishad Hossain provides a valuable wicket-taking option through the middle overs with his attacking approach. Bangladesh’s bowling attack looked balanced and disciplined in the opening match, keeping Pakistan under constant pressure and ensuring the target never grew beyond reach. Transition phase for Pakistan - For Pakistan, this series represents the beginning of a transitional phase. The visitors arrived in Bangladesh with a new-look squad that excluded several established names, including Babar Azam, Saim Ayub and Mohammad Nawaz, while Shaheen Shah Afridi leads a side featuring multiple debutants trying to establish themselves at the international level. One of the young players attracting attention is Maaz Sadaqat, who was named Player of the Tournament at the 2025 ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars in Doha and is regarded as one of Pakistan's promising emerging talents and showed glimpses of his talent in the first game. Their biggest concern from the first ODI was the fragile batting display, with only Faheem Ashraf and Sahibzada Farhan showing resistance as the rest of the lineup struggled against disciplined bowling. Pakistan search for stability - Pakistan will need stronger contributions from the likes of Salman Ali Agha and Mohammad Rizwan, whose experience in the middle order could prove vital in stabilising the innings, while Mohammad Wasim adds value as a lower-order hitter alongside his pace with the ball.
